preamble: Excrescence of [p] inserts a voiceless labial stop between the labial nasal [m] and a following voiceless obstruent (typically [s], [t] or [θ]). The stop arises when the velum rises before the lips open, producing an oral release with the place of [m] and the voicelessness of the next consonant. English shows it both historically (Old English ǣmtiġ > empty, Middle English glimsen > glimpse) and as a variable modern pronunciation (warmth [wɔːmpθ], hamster [ˈhæmpstə]); Classical Latin inserted p regularly in m.s and m.t clusters (emō → ēmptus, sūmō → sūmpsī, contemnō → contemptus).
